title: त्रिषष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 63 · Vrishasena's death and Karna's grief

summary.en: Seeing Vrishasena killed, Karna, filled with grief and anger, turns toward Arjuna, and Shalya warns him of the dangers. Karna replies that he will fight Arjuna and tells Shalya to drive on.
summary.kn: ವೃಷಸೇನ ಹತನಾದುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡ ಕರ್ಣ ದುಃಖ-ಕೋಪದಿಂದ ಅರ್ಜುನನತ್ತ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಶಲ್ಯ ಅಪಾಯಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಎಚ್ಚರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ತಾನು ಅರ್ಜುನನೊಡನೆ ಹೋರಾಡುವೆನೆಂದು ಕರ್ಣ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿ ನಡೆಸಲು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: वृषसेन को मरा देखकर शोक और क्रोध से भरा कर्ण अर्जुन की ओर मुड़ता है, और शल्य उसे खतरों से चेताता है। कर्ण उत्तर देता है कि वह अर्जुन से लड़ेगा और शल्य को रथ बढ़ाने को कहता है।
summary.te: వృషసేనుడు చంపబడటం చూసి దుఃఖం, కోపంతో నిండిన కర్ణుడు అర్జునుని వైపు తిరుగుతాడు; శల్యుడు ప్రమాదాల గురించి హెచ్చరిస్తాడు. తాను అర్జునునితో పోరాడతానని కర్ణుడు బదులిచ్చి రథం నడపమంటాడు.
summary.ta: விருஷசேனன் கொல்லப்பட்டதைக் கண்ட கர்ணன் துயரமும் சினமும் நிறைந்து அர்ஜுனனை நோக்கித் திரும்ப, சல்யன் ஆபத்துகளை எச்சரிக்கிறான். அர்ஜுனனுடன் போரிடுவேன் என்று கர்ணன் கூறி, தேரைச் செலுத்தச் சொல்கிறான்.
summary.ml: വൃഷസേനൻ കൊല്ലപ്പെടുന്നത് കണ്ട കർണ്ണൻ ദുഃഖവും കോപവും നിറഞ്ഞ് അർജുനനു നേരെ തിരിയുന്നു; അപകടങ്ങളെക്കുറിച്ച് ശല്യൻ മുന്നറിയിപ്പ് നൽകുന്നു. അർജുനനോട് പൊരുതുമെന്നും രഥം മുന്നോട്ടു തെളിക്കാനും കർണ്ണൻ ശല്യനോട് മറുപടി പറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.63; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
वृषसेनं हतं दृष्ट्वा शोकामर्षसमन्वितः ।
मुक्त्वा शोकोद्भवं वारि नेत्राभ्यां सहसा वृषः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Vrishasena slain, Karna, filled with grief and anger, suddenly let fall tears of sorrow from his eyes.

verses.text:
रथेन कर्णस्तेजस्वी जगामाभिमुखो रिपून् ।
युद्धायामर्षताम्राक्षः समाहूय धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: Radiant Karna, his eyes red with fury, challenged Dhananjaya and drove his chariot toward his enemies to fight.

verses.text:
तौ रथौ सूर्यसंकाशौ वैयाघ्रपरिवारणौ ।
समेतौ ददृशुस्तत्र द्वाविवार्कौ समागतौ ॥

meaning.en: Those two chariots, bright as the sun and covered with tiger skins, were seen meeting there like two suns come together.

verses.text:
श्वेताश्वौ पुरुषादित्यावास्थितावरिमर्दनौ ।
शुशुभाते महात्मानौ चन्द्रादित्यौ यथा दिवि ॥

meaning.en: With white horses, those two men, like suns among men and crushers of foes, stood in their chariots and shone like the moon and sun in the sky.

verses.text:
तौ दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं जग्मुः सर्वभूतानि मारिष ।
त्रैलोक्यविजये यत्ताविन्द्रवैरोचनाविव ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them, O lord, all beings were filled with wonder, as the two were bent on conquering the three worlds like Indra and Virochana's son.

verses.text:
रथज्यातलनिर्ह्रादैर्बाणशङ्खरवैरपि ।
तौ रथावभिधावन्तौ समालोक्य महीक्षिताम् ॥

meaning.en: When the kings saw the two chariots rushing on with the roar of wheels, bowstrings, palms, arrows and conches,

verses.text:
ध्वजौ च दृष्ट्वा संसक्तौ विस्मयः समपद्यत ।
हस्तिकक्ष्यां च कर्णस्य वानरं च किरीटिनः ॥

meaning.en: and saw the two banners locked together, wonder arose: Karna's elephant rope and the diadem-wearer's ape.

verses.text:
तौ रथौ संप्रसक्तौ च दृष्ट्वा भारत पार्थिवाः ।
सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुः साधुवादांश्च पुष्कलान् ॥

meaning.en: O Bharata, seeing those two chariots engaged, the kings raised lion-roars and shouted many cheers.

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु द्वैरथं ताभ्यां तत्र योधाः समन्ततः ।
चक्रुर्बाहुवलं चैव तथा चेलवलं महत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing of the duel of chariots between the two, the warriors on every side slapped their arms and waved great cloths.

verses.text:
आजग्मुः कुरवस्तत्र वादित्रानुगतास्तदा ।
कर्णं प्रहर्षयन्तश्च शङ्खान्दध्मुश्च पुष्कलान् ॥

meaning.en: The Kurus came there with their musicians in attendance, cheering Karna on and blowing many conches.

verses.text:
तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे हर्षयन्तो धनंजयम् ।
तूर्यशङ्खनिनादेन दिशः सर्वा व्यनादयन् ॥

meaning.en: In the same way all the Pandavas, rejoicing in Dhananjaya, made every quarter ring with the sound of horns and conches.

verses.text:
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितोत्क्रुष्टैस्तुमुलं सर्वतोऽभवत् ।
बाहुघोषाश्च वीराणां कर्णार्जुनसमागमे ॥

meaning.en: There was a tumult on every side, with whoops, claps and shouts, and the drumming of the heroes' arms, at the meeting of Karna and Arjuna.

verses.text:
तौ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रौ रथस्थौ रथिनां वरौ ।
प्रगृहीतमहाचापौ शरशक्तिगदायुधौ ॥

meaning.en: Seeing those two tigers among men, best of chariot-warriors, standing in their chariots with great bows ready, and arrows, darts and maces as weapons,

verses.text:
वर्मिणौ बद्धनिस्त्रिंशौ श्वेताश्वौ शङ्खशोभिनौ ।
तूणीरवरसंपन्नौ द्वावपि स्म सुदर्शनौ ॥

meaning.en: armored, with swords bound on, white-horsed and splendid with conches, with fine quivers, both were very beautiful to see,

verses.text:
रक्तचन्दनदिग्धाङ्गौ समदौ वृषभाविव ।
आशीविषसमप्रख्यौ यमकालान्तकोपमौ ॥

meaning.en: their limbs smeared with red sandal paste, wild like two bulls in rut, like venomous serpents, like Yama, Time and the Ender,

verses.text:
इन्द्रवृत्राविव क्रुद्धौ सूर्याचन्द्रमसप्रभौ ।
महाग्रहाविव क्रूरौ युगान्ते समुपस्थितौ ॥

meaning.en: enraged like Indra and Vritra, bright as the sun and moon, cruel as two great planets come at the end of the age:

verses.text:
देवगर्भौ देवसमौ देवतुल्यौ च रूपतः ।
समेतौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ प्रेक्ष्य कर्णधनंजयौ ॥

meaning.en: they seemed born of gods, equal to gods, like gods in form: so Karna and Dhananjaya, two tigers among men, appeared as they met.

verses.text:
उभौ वरायुधधरावुभौ रणकृतश्रमौ ।
उभौ च बाहुशब्देन नादयन्तौ नभस्तलम् ॥

meaning.en: Both bore the finest weapons, both were weary of no battle, both made the sky resound with the slapping of their arms.

verses.text:
उभौ विश्रुतकर्माणौ पौरुषेण बलेन च ।
उभौ च सदृशौ युद्धे शम्बरामरराजयोः ॥

meaning.en: Both were famed in deeds, for manliness and strength; both were equal in battle to Shambara and to the king of the immortals.

verses.text:
कार्तवीर्यसमौ युद्धे तथा दाशरथेः समौ ।
विष्णुवीर्यसमौ वीर्ये तथा भवसमौ युधि ॥

meaning.en: In battle they were like Kartavirya, like Dasharatha's son Rama, like Vishnu in valor and like Bhava in the fight.

verses.text:
उभौ श्वेतहयौ राजन्रथप्रवरवाहिनौ ।
सारथी प्रवरौ चैव तयोरास्तां महाबलौ ॥

meaning.en: Both, O king, had white horses and the best of chariots to carry them, and each had an excellent and very strong charioteer.

verses.text:
तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महाराज राजमानौ महारथौ ।
सिद्धचारणसंघानां विस्मयः समपद्यत ॥

meaning.en: Seeing those two great chariot-warriors shining, great king, wonder arose among the hosts of Siddhas and Charanas.

verses.text:
धार्तराष्ट्रास्ततः कर्णं सबला भरतर्षभ ।
परिवव्रुर्महात्मानं क्षिप्रमाहवशोभिनम् ॥

meaning.en: Then, O best of the Bharatas, the Dhritarashtrians with their forces quickly surrounded the great-souled Karna, shining in battle.

verses.text:
तथैव पाण्डवा हृष्टा धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः ।
परिवव्रुर्महात्मानं पार्थमप्रतिमं युधि ॥

meaning.en: In the same way the delighted Pandavas, led by Dhrishtadyumna, surrounded the great-souled Partha, matchless in the fight.

verses.text:
तावकानां रणे कर्णो ग्लह आसीद्विशां पते ।
तथैव पाण्डवेयानां ग्लहः पार्थोऽभवद्युधि ॥

meaning.en: O lord of people, Karna was the stake of your side in that battle, and Partha was the stake of the Pandavas in the fight.

verses.text:
त एव सभ्यास्तत्रासन्प्रेक्षकाश्चाभवन्स्म ते ।
तत्रैषां ग्लहमानानां ध्रुवौ जयपराजयौ ॥

meaning.en: They themselves were the assembly members there and they were the onlookers; for them as they wagered, victory and defeat were fixed.

verses.text:
ताभ्यां द्यूतं समायत्तं विजयायेतराय वा ।
अस्माकं पाण्डवानां च स्थितानां रणमूर्धनि ॥

meaning.en: The dice-game was staked on those two, for victory or the opposite, for us and for the Pandavas standing at the head of the battle.

verses.text:
तौ तु स्थितौ महाराज समरे युद्धशालिनौ ।
अन्योन्यं प्रतिसंरब्धावन्योन्यस्य जयैषिणौ ॥

meaning.en: Both stood there in the battle, O great king, proud in fighting, each enraged at the other and each wishing the other's defeat.

verses.text:
तावुभौ प्रजिहीर्षेतामिन्द्रवृत्राविवाभितः ।
भीमरूपधरावास्तां महाधूमाविव ग्रहौ ॥

meaning.en: Both wished to strike each other all around, like Indra and Vritra, and both took fearsome form, like two great smoky planets.

verses.text:
ततोऽन्तरिक्षे साक्षेपा विवादा भरतर्षभ ।
मिथो भेदाश्च भूतानामासन्कर्णार्जुनान्तरे ।
व्याश्रयन्त दिशो भिन्नाः सर्वलोकाश्च मारिष ॥

meaning.en: Then in the sky, O best of the Bharatas, there arose taunting disputes and divisions among the beings between Karna and Arjuna; the quarters were split and all the worlds took sides, my lord.

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः ।
प्रतिपक्षग्रहं चक्रुः कर्णार्जुनसमागमे ॥

meaning.en: Gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Pishachas, serpents and Rakshasas took opposing sides at the meeting of Karna and Arjuna.

verses.text:
द्यौरासीत्कर्णतो व्यग्रा सनक्षत्रा विशां पते ।
भूमिर्विशाला पार्थस्य माता पुत्रस्य भारत ॥

meaning.en: The sky with its stars, lord of people, was anxious on Karna's side, while the broad earth, as a mother for her son, was on Partha's side.

verses.text:
सरितः सागराश्चैव गिरयश्च नरोत्तम ।
वृक्षाश्चौषधयस्तत्र व्याश्रयन्त किरीटिनम् ॥

meaning.en: Rivers, oceans, mountains, trees and herbs, best of men, took refuge there with the diadem-wearer.

verses.text:
असुरा यातुधानाश्च गुह्यकाश्च परंतप ।
कर्णतः समपद्यन्त खेचराणि वयांसि च ॥

meaning.en: Asuras, Yatudhanas, Guhyakas and birds that fly in the sky came out on Karna's side, O scorcher of foes.

verses.text:
रत्नानि निधयः सर्वे वेदाश्चाख्यानपञ्चमाः ।
सोपवेदोपनिषदः सरहस्याः ससंग्रहाः ॥

meaning.en: Jewels, treasures, all the Vedas with the Itihasa as the fifth, with the Upavedas, Upanishads, secret teachings and compendia,

verses.text:
वासुकिश्चित्रसेनश्च तक्षकश्चोपतक्षकः ।
पर्वताश्च तथा सर्वे काद्रवेयाश्च सान्वयाः ।
विषवन्तो महारोषा नागाश्चार्जुनतोऽभवन् ॥

meaning.en: Vasuki, Chitrasena, Takshaka and Upatakshaka, and all the mountains, and the sons of Kadru with their lines, the venomous and furious serpents, were on Arjuna's side.

verses.text:
ऐरावताः सौरभेया वैशालेयाश्च भोगिनः ।
एतेऽभवन्नर्जुनतः क्षुद्रसर्पास्तु कर्णतः ॥

meaning.en: The Airavatas, Saurabheyas and Vaishaleyas, the hooded snakes, were on Arjuna's side, while the petty snakes were on Karna's.

verses.text:
ईहामृगा व्याडमृगा मङ्गल्याश्च मृगद्विजाः ।
पार्थस्य विजयं राजन्सर्व एवाभिसंश्रिताः ॥

meaning.en: Wolf-like beasts, beasts of prey, auspicious deer and birds all took refuge in Partha's victory, O king.

verses.text:
वसवो मरुतः साध्या रुद्रा विश्वेऽश्विनौ तथा ।
अग्निरिन्द्रश्च सोमश्च पवनश्च दिशो दश ।
धनंजयमुपाजग्मुरादित्याः कर्णतोऽभवन् ॥

meaning.en: The Vasus, Maruts, Sadhyas, Rudras, Vishvadevas, the Ashvins, Agni, Indra, Soma, Pavana and the ten quarters came to Dhananjaya; the Adityas were on Karna's side.

verses.text:
देवास्तु पितृभिः सार्धं सगणार्जुनतोऽभवन् ।
यमो वैश्रवणश्चैव वरुणश्च यतोऽर्जुनः ॥

meaning.en: The gods with the Pitris and their hosts were on Arjuna's side; so were Yama, Vaishravana and Varuna, wherever Arjuna was.

verses.text:
देवब्रह्मनृपर्षीणां गणाः पाण्डवतोऽभवन् ।
तुम्बुरुप्रमुखा राजन्गन्धर्वाश्च यतोऽर्जुनः ॥

meaning.en: The hosts of gods, brahmins and royal sages were on the Pandava's side, O king, and the Gandharvas headed by Tumburu were where Arjuna was.

verses.text:
प्रावेयाः सह मौनेयैर्गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ।
ईहामृगव्याडमृगैर्द्विपाश्च रथपत्तिभिः ॥

meaning.en: The Praveyas with the Mauneyas, hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases, with wolf-like beasts and beasts of prey, elephants, chariots and foot soldiers,

verses.text:
उह्यमानास्तथा मेघैर्वायुना च मनीषिणः ।
दिदृक्षवः समाजग्मुः कर्णार्जुनसमागमम् ॥

meaning.en: and the wise ones carried by clouds and wind, gathered, eager to see the meeting of Karna and Arjuna.

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वा नागा यक्षाः पतत्रिणः ।
महर्षयो वेदविदः पितरश्च स्वधाभुजः ॥

meaning.en: Gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, serpents, Yakshas, birds, great seers who know the Vedas, and the Pitris who feed on svadha,

verses.text:
तपो विद्यास्तथौषध्यो नानारूपाम्बरत्विषः ।
अन्तरिक्षे महाराज विनदन्तोऽवतस्थिरे ॥

meaning.en: austerity, learning, herbs, and beings of many forms and shining garments stood in the sky, great king, shouting.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मर्षिभिः सार्धं प्रजापतिभिरेव च ।
भवेनावस्थितो यानं दिव्यं तं देशमभ्ययात् ॥

meaning.en: Brahma, with the Brahmarshis and the Prajapatis, came to that place, with Bhava, seated on his divine vehicle.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा प्रजापतिं देवाः स्वयंभुवमुपागमन् ।
समोऽस्तु देव विजय एतयोर्नरसिंहयोः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the Lord of creatures, the gods approached the Self-born and said, "O God, let the victory of these two lions among men be equal."

verses.text:
तदुपश्रुत्य मघवा प्रणिपत्य पितामहम् ।
कर्णार्जुनविनाशेन मा नश्यत्वखिलं जगत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing that, Indra bowed to the Grandsire and said, "Let not the whole world perish through the destruction of Karna and Arjuna.

verses.text:
स्वयंभो ब्रूहि तद्वाक्यं समोऽस्तु विजयोऽनयोः ।
तत्तथास्तु नमस्तेऽस्तु प्रसीद भगवन्मम ॥

meaning.en: Self-born, speak that word, that the victory of these two be equal." "So be it. Honor to you; be gracious to me, Lord."

verses.text:
ब्रह्मेशानावथो वाक्यमूचतुस्त्रिदशेश्वरम् ।
विजयो ध्रुव एवास्तु विजयस्य महात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: Then Brahma and Ishana spoke these words to the lord of the thirty gods: "Let the victory of the great-souled Vijaya, Arjuna, be certain.

verses.text:
मनस्वी बलवाञ्शूरः कृतास्त्रश्च तपोधनः ।
बिभर्ति च महातेजा धनुर्वेदमशेषतः ॥

meaning.en: He is intelligent, strong, brave, trained in weapons, rich in austerity, of great splendor, and he holds the whole science of the bow.

verses.text:
अतिक्रमेच्च माहात्म्याद्दिष्टमेतस्य पर्ययात् ।
अतिक्रान्ते च लोकानामभावो नियतो भवेत् ॥

meaning.en: By his greatness he could overstep what is fated for him by a turn of destiny, and if that is overstepped, the end of the worlds is certain.

verses.text:
न विद्यते व्यवस्थानं कृष्णयोः क्रुद्धयोः क्वचित् ।
स्रष्टारौ ह्यसतश्चोभौ सतश्च पुरुषर्षभौ ॥

meaning.en: When the two Krishnas are angry, nothing anywhere stands firm; for both bulls among men are makers of the unreal and the real.

verses.text:
नरनारायणावेतौ पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ ।
अनियत्तौ नियन्तारावभीतौ स्म परंतपौ ॥

meaning.en: They are Nara and Narayana, ancient and the best of seers, unrestrained yet restrainers, fearless, scorchers of foes.

verses.text:
कर्णो लोकानयं मुख्यान्प्राप्नोतु पुरुषर्षभः ।
वीरो वैकर्तनः शूरो विजयस्त्वस्तु कृष्णयोः ॥

meaning.en: Let Karna, bull among men, the brave son of Vikartana, win the foremost worlds; but let victory belong to the two Krishnas.

verses.text:
वसूनां च सलोकत्वं मरुतां वा समाप्नुयात् ।
सहितो द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां नाकलोके महीयताम् ॥

meaning.en: Let him attain the worlds of the Vasus, or of the Maruts, and with Drona and Bhishma be honored in the world of heaven."

verses.text:
इत्युक्तो देवदेवाभ्यां सहस्राक्षोऽब्रवीद्वचः ।
आमन्त्र्य सर्वभूतानि ब्रह्मेशानानुशासनात् ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed by the two gods of gods, the thousand-eyed Indra, at the command of Brahma and Ishana, addressed all beings.

verses.text:
श्रुतं भवद्भिर्यत्प्रोक्तं भगवद्भ्यां जगद्धितम् ।
तत्तथा नान्यथा तद्धि तिष्ठध्वं गतमन्यवः ॥

meaning.en: "You have heard what the two lords said for the good of the world; it will be so and not otherwise. Stay, your anger set aside."

verses.text:
इति श्रुत्वेन्द्रवचनं सर्वभूतानि मारिष ।
विस्मितान्यभवन्राजन्पूजयां चक्रिरे च तत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Indra's words, all beings, my lord, were amazed, O king, and honored them.

verses.text:
व्यसृजंश्च सुगन्धीनि नानारूपाणि खात्तथा ।
पुष्पवर्षाणि विबुधा देवतूर्याण्यवादयन् ॥

meaning.en: The gods let fall showers of fragrant flowers of many kinds from the sky and sounded divine trumpets.

verses.text:
दिदृक्षवश्चाप्रतिमं द्वैरथं नरसिंहयोः ।
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः सर्व एवावतस्थिरे ।
रथौ च तौ श्वेतहयौ युक्तकेतू महास्वनौ ॥

meaning.en: Wishing to see the matchless chariot duel of those two lions among men, gods, Danavas and Gandharvas all stood by; and those two chariots with white horses, with banners raised, roared mightily.

verses.text:
समागता लोकवीराः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ।
वासुदेवार्जुनौ वीरौ कर्णशल्यौ च भारत ॥

meaning.en: The heroes of the world who had gathered blew their conches, each separately: the heroes Vasudeva and Arjuna, and Karna and Shalya, O Bharata.

verses.text:
तद्भीरुसंत्रासकरं युद्धं समभवत्तदा ।
अन्योन्यस्पर्धिनोर्वीर्ये शक्रशम्बरयोरिव ॥

meaning.en: Then there came a battle that frightened the timid, between two men rivaling each other in prowess, like Indra and Shambara.

verses.text:
तयोर्ध्वजौ वीतमालौ शुशुभाते रथस्थितौ ।
पृथग्रूपौ समार्छन्तौ क्रोधं युद्धे परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: Their banners, wearing garlands, shone on the chariots; they were different in form, and each increased wrath against the other in the battle.

verses.text:
कर्णस्याशीविषनिभा रत्नसारवती दृढा ।
पुरंदरधनुःप्रख्या हस्तिकक्ष्या व्यराजत ॥

meaning.en: Karna's elephant rope, strong, rich in gems, like a venomous serpent and like Indra's bow, shone out.

verses.text:
कपिश्रेष्ठस्तु पार्थस्य व्यादितास्यो भयंकरः ।
भीषयन्नेव दंष्ट्राभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यो रविर्यथा ॥

meaning.en: But Partha's ape, the best of apes, terrible with open mouth, frightening with its fangs, hard to look at like the sun,

verses.text:
युद्धाभिलाषुको भूत्वा ध्वजो गाण्डीवधन्वनः ।
कर्णध्वजमुपातिष्ठत्सोऽवदीदभिनर्दयन् ॥

meaning.en: the banner of the wielder of the Gandiva, became eager for battle, approached Karna's banner and roared, yelling.

verses.text:
उत्पत्य च महावेगः कक्ष्यामभ्यहनत्कपिः ।
नखैश्च दशनैश्चैव गरुडः पन्नगं यथा ॥

meaning.en: Leaping with great speed, the ape struck the rope with its nails and teeth, as Garuda strikes a snake.

verses.text:
सुकिङ्किणीकाभरणा कालपाशोपमायसी ।
अभ्यद्रवत्सुसंक्रुद्धा नागकक्ष्या महाकपिम् ॥

meaning.en: The iron elephant rope, with fine tinkling bells like the noose of Time, furiously rushed at the great ape.

verses.text:
उभयोरुत्तमे युद्धे द्वैरथे द्यूत आहृते ।
प्रकुर्वाते ध्वजौ युद्धं प्रत्यहेषन्हयान्हयाः ॥

meaning.en: In that best of double-chariot duels, the dice-game now brought on, the two banners fought and the horses neighed at horses.

verses.text:
अविध्यत्पुण्डरीकाक्षः शल्यं नयनसायकैः ।
स चापि पुण्डरीकाक्षं तथैवाभिसमैक्षत ॥

meaning.en: The lotus-eyed Krishna pierced Shalya with arrows of his eyes, and Shalya looked back at the lotus-eyed one in the same way.

verses.text:
तत्राजयद्वासुदेवः शल्यं नयनसायकैः ।
कर्णं चाप्यजयद्दृष्ट्या कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः ॥

meaning.en: There Vasudeva defeated Shalya with the arrows of his eyes, and Dhananjaya, son of Kunti, defeated Karna with his glance.

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीत्सूतपुत्रः शल्यमाभाष्य सस्मितम् ।
यदि पार्थो रणे हन्यादद्य मामिह कर्हिचित् ।
किमुत्तरं तदा ते स्यात्सखे सत्यं ब्रवीहि मे ॥

meaning.en: Then the charioteer's son said to Shalya with a smile: "If Partha should ever kill me here in battle today, what will your answer be, friend? Tell me truly."

verses.text: शल्य उवाच

meaning.en: Shalya said:

verses.text:
यदि कर्ण रणे हन्यादद्य त्वां श्वेतवाहनः ।
उभावेकरथेनाहं हन्यां माधवपाण्डवौ ॥

meaning.en: "Karna, if the white-horsed Arjuna kills you in battle today, I will kill both Madhava and the Pandava in a single chariot."

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
एवमेव तु गोविंदमर्जुनः प्रत्यभाषत ।
तं प्रहस्याब्रवीत्कृष्णः पार्थं परमिदं वचः ॥

meaning.en: In the same way Arjuna answered Govinda; and Krishna, laughing, said these superior words to Partha.

verses.text:
पतेद्दिवाकरः स्थानाच्छीर्येतानेकधा क्षितिः ।
शैत्यमग्निरियान्न त्वा कर्णो हन्याद्धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: "The sun may fall from its place, the earth may split in many ways, fire may become cold, but Karna will not kill you, Dhananjaya.

verses.text:
यदि त्वेवं कथंचित्स्याल्लोकपर्यसनं यथा ।
हन्यां कर्णं तथा शल्यं बाहुभ्यामेव संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Yet if somehow it came about, like the ruin of the world, I would kill Karna and Shalya in battle with my bare arms."

verses.text:
इति कृष्णवचः श्रुत्वा प्रहसन्कपिकेतनः ।
अर्जुनः प्रत्युवाचेदं कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम् ।
ममाप्येतावपर्याप्तौ कर्णशल्यौ जनार्दन ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Krishna's words, the ape-bannered Arjuna laughed and answered Krishna, who works without effort: "Karna and Shalya together are not enough even for me, Janardana.

verses.text:
सपताकाध्वजं कर्णं सशल्यरथवाजिनम् ।
सच्छत्रकवचं चैव सशक्तिशरकार्मुकम् ॥

meaning.en: Today you will see Karna, with his banner and flag, Shalya, his chariot and horses, his umbrella, armor, dart, arrows and bow,

verses.text:
द्रष्टास्यद्य शरैः कर्णं रणे कृत्तमनेकधा ।
अद्यैनं सरथं साश्वं सशक्तिकवचायुधम् ।
न हि मे शाम्यते वैरं कृष्णां यत्प्राहसत्पुरा ॥

meaning.en: cut into many pieces in the fight by my arrows; today I will deal with him with his chariot, horses, dart, armor and weapons. My enmity is not quiet, because he laughed at Krishna in the past.

verses.text:
अद्य द्रष्टासि गोविन्द कर्णमुन्मथितं मया ।
वारणेनेव मत्तेन पुष्पितं जगतीरुहम् ॥

meaning.en: Today, Govinda, you will see Karna uprooted by me, like a blossoming tree uprooted by a rutting elephant.

verses.text:
अद्य ता मधुरा वाचः श्रोतासि मधुसूदन ।
अद्याभिमन्युजननीमनृणः सान्त्वयिष्यसि ।
कुन्तीं पितृष्वसारं च संप्रहृष्टो जनार्दन ॥

meaning.en: Today, Madhusudana, you will hear those sweet words, and today, free of debt, delighted, Janardana, you will comfort Abhimanyu's mother and Kunti, your father's sister.

verses.text:
अद्य बाष्पमुखीं कृष्णां सान्त्वयिष्यसि माधव ।
वाग्भिश्चामृतकल्पाभिर्धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥

meaning.en: Today, Madhava, you will comfort Krishna, her face wet with tears, and Yudhishthira, king of dharma, with words like nectar."
